blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Choosing between transport modes in practice is rarely a clean textbook decision. Most real shipments come with constraints: a customer who has promised their own customer a date, a product that cannot sit in a container for three weeks, a budget that has already been spent on something else, a port that is running at capacity.

Good logisticians build a short mental checklist. What is the true deadline — not the friendly one on the contract? What is the volume and weight? How sensitive is the product to heat, vibration, or delay? What modes have capacity this week, and at what price?

The more constraints you have, the fewer options remain. Usually one mode is clearly right, one is clearly wrong, and one is a painful compromise. The real skill is explaining, in one sentence, why you chose the one you did.

items.q: According to the text, why is choosing a transport mode rarely a clean decision?
options: Because customers never set a date
Because real shipments come with constraints
items.why: "rarely a clean textbook decision. Most real shipments come with constraints."

items.q: What does the text say about the 'true deadline'?
options: It may differ from the friendly one on the contract
It is decided by the product itself
It is always written in the contract
It is set by the port
items.why: "the true deadline — not the friendly one on the contract": o prazo real pode não ser o do contrato.

items.q: According to the text, what happens as the number of constraints increases?
items.why: "The more constraints you have, the fewer options remain."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: The right mode should be justified in a single sentence.
Capacity this week is part of the decision.
The best mode is simply the cheapest one available.
Product sensitivity affects the mode you choose.
items.why: Inferência: o texto trata prazo, sensibilidade e capacidade — não reduz a escolha só ao preço.

items.q: The mention of a 'painful compromise' suggests that…
options: at least one available option satisfies no constraint well
every shipment has a perfect mode
compromises are always the cheapest choice
items.why: Inferência: o compromisso doloroso é a opção que não atende bem nenhuma restrição, mas ainda está na mesa.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver orientando o novo coordenador. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, let's walk through this one together before you book anything. We have a temperature-sensitive shipment, a tight deadline, and a tight budget — so all three of the hard constraints at once. Don't panic; that usually means the answer is closer than you think.

You've got three options on the table. Air is fast enough and keeps the product cold, but it eats the whole budget and then some. Sea is well inside budget and handles the volume beautifully, but it takes three weeks — the product simply won't survive that. Road with a refrigerated trailer sits in the middle: it protects the temperature, it lands a day inside the deadline, and it's expensive, but not impossible.

So notice what just happened. Once you're honest about the real deadline and the fact that the product can't sit in a warm box for weeks, sea drops out. Air is right on speed but wrong on cost. That leaves the refrigerated road option as your painful compromise.

Now here's the part I want you to practise. Write me one sentence — just one — explaining why you chose it. If you can't justify it in a sentence, you haven't really made the decision yet.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What three constraints does Oliver say apply to this shipment?
options: Temperature sensitivity, a tight deadline, and a tight budget
items.why: "a temperature-sensitive shipment, a tight deadline, and a tight budget."

items.q: Why does Oliver rule out the sea option?
options: It takes three weeks and the product won't survive
It arrives after the port closes
items.why: "it takes three weeks — the product simply won't survive that."

items.q: What is the problem with the air option, according to Oliver?
options: It cannot keep the product cold
It eats the whole budget and then some
items.why: "Air is right on speed but wrong on cost… it eats the whole budget and then some."

items.q: When Oliver says 'that usually means the answer is closer than you think', he is suggesting that…
options: tight budgets always mean cancelling the shipment
there is never a good answer under pressure
the coordinator should ask a manager instead
more constraints often narrow the choice to one clear option
items.why: Inferência: quanto mais restrições, menos opções sobram — a decisão fica mais evidente.

items.q: Why does Oliver ask for a one-sentence justification?
options: To compare it against the contract wording
Because the budget requires written approval
Because a choice you can't justify simply hasn't really been made
To keep the paperwork short for the client
items.why: Inferência: "If you can't justify it in a sentence, you haven't really made the decision yet."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Budget is the tightest constraint on this order." A constraint is…
options: a limitation you must work within
items.why: Constraint = restrição: um limite dentro do qual você tem de operar.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "This cargo is highly ___ to heat, so we cannot risk a slow mode."
items.why: Sensitive = sensível: reage mal ao calor, exigindo transporte cuidadoso.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Sea freight became attractive once we saw the sheer ___ of the order — thousands of pallets."
items.why: Volume = volume: a grande quantidade favorece o transporte marítimo.

items.q: "The port has no spare capacity this week." Capacity here means…
options: the ability to take on more shipments
items.why: Capacity = capacidade: quanto o porto ainda consegue movimentar.

items.q: "Road was neither cheapest nor fastest — it was a compromise." A compromise is…
options: a middle option that gives up something on each side
items.why: Compromise = concessão: uma solução intermediária que cede em algo de cada lado.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem ao decidir modais de transporte. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager still has to sign off on the refrigerated road quote." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Sea freight drops out once you're honest about the deadline." To drop out means to…
items.why: Drop out = sair da disputa, deixar de ser uma opção viável.

items.q: "Let's weigh up air against refrigerated road before booking." To weigh up means to…
items.why: Weigh up = ponderar, comparar vantagens e desvantagens.

items.q: "Booking sea to save money could backfire if the product spoils." To backfire means to…
options: produce the opposite of the intended result
items.why: Backfire = sair pela culatra: produzir o efeito contrário ao pretendido.

items.q: "Planning a week earlier would free up cheaper options." To free up means to…
items.why: Free up = liberar, tornar disponível — mais tempo abre opções mais baratas.
